<div><tool-result call-id="call_IdPQNXg84N08h1PAcxCgx71X"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 16.5KB, 266 lines, showing lines 1-266]\n1\t# Positron package commands\n2\t\n3\tReading,...[truncated, total 17927 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 16.5KB, 266 lines, showing lines 1-266]\n# Positron package commands\n\nReading, installing and updating the packages in an interpreter session. See\n[SKILL.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/SKILL.md) for how to call these commands and how to\nhandle failures.\n\nThe **Arguments** and **Returns** entries below are generated from the running\nbuild's command metadata, so they always match this Positron. The surrounding\nguidance is hand-written.\n\n## Read the environment, never probe it\n\nTo find out what is installed, what version it is, or whether something newer\nis available, call `positronPackages.getAllPackages` (the whole environment) or\n`positronPackages.getPackages` (specific packages, by name). **Do not run code\nto find out.** Writing `import pandas` in a try/except, calling `pip list`,\n`installed.packages()`, `importlib.metadata.version()`, or anything similar\nthrough `executeCode` is the wrong move every time: it runs code the user did\nnot ask for, it can have side effects (an import executes module-level code),\nit only answers for the one package you thought to test, and it tells you\nnothing about whether a newer version exists.\n\nThese commands have none of those problems. They change nothing, show the user\nnothing, and need no pane open. Reach for one before any package operation, and\nbefore answering any question about what the session has.\n\n**Which of the two to call:**\n\n- To size up the environment, or list what is installed, call\n  `getAllPackages`. It returns a compact entry per package, built to fit\n  hundreds of packages at once.\n- To look a package (or a few) up by name -- its full detail, its security\n  vulnerabilities, or simply *whether it is installed at all* -- call\n  `getPackages` with the names. A named package that is missing comes back in\n  `notFound`, which is a definitive \"not installed\"; the compact list can be\n  large, so do not conclude a package is absent just because you did not spot\n  it there.\n\n## Reading what's installed\n\n### `positronPackages.getAllPackages`\n\nReports every package installed in the foreground session, each with its\ninstalled version and whether a newer one is available. A **compact** list: the\n`description` is shortened to 256 characters (suffixed with `...` when cut), and\nsecurity vulnerabilities and the per-package detail fields (license, author,\nsource repository, publication date) are left out entirely to keep the whole\nenvironment inside the token budget. When you need the full description, the\ndetail fields, or the vulnerabilities for a package, call `getPackages` with its\nname.\n\nRead-only and quiet. Unlike the write commands below, this has **no\nprecondition** -- it is always callable, and tells you in its payload when it\nhas nothing to say. So a `disabled` failure from a write command does not mean\nyou cannot read.\n\n**Reading the payload:**\n\n- `available: false` comes with a `reason`, and each one calls for a different\n  response:\n  - `disabled` -- the user turned the Packages pane off in settings. Say so;\n    do not offer to turn it on by running code.\n  - `no-session` -- nothing is running, so there is no environment to\n    describe. Ask the user to start an interpreter.\n  - `session-not-ready` -- a session is starting up (or has exited). This one\n    is worth retrying shortly; the others are not.\n  - `unsupported` -- this runtime has no package manager. Nothing here will\n    work for it.\n  - `failed` -- the read itself failed; relay `message` rather than guessing.\n- `metadataStatus` says how far `outdated` can be trusted. Only `fresh` means\n  the repositories were queried just now. On `cached`, `timed-out` or\n  `fetch-failed`, report update information as possibly stale rather than\n  telling the user they are up to date. On `unsupported`, no package has\n  `outdated` at all, so its absence means nothing.\n- `session` names the session the answer describes. It is one session's\n  environment, not the machine's -- do not carry an answer across a session\n  switch or apply it to a different language.\n- `attached` is not the same as installed. A package can be installed but not\n  attached (not `library()`d in R, not imported in Python). \"Is pandas\n  available?\" is answered by the package appearing in the list at all;\n  `attached` only says whether it is on the search path right now.\n\n**Arguments:** None.\n\n**Returns:** An object with available: true, the session the packages belong to, the installed packages (name, version, latestVersion, outdated, attached, description, url) -- where description is shortened to 256 characters and suffixed with \"...\" when cut -- and metadataStatus saying how the outdated state was obtained: 'fresh' (repositories queried now), 'cached' (as of the last fetch), 'unsupported' (this runtime reports no outdated state, so no package has it), 'timed-out' (the list is complete but outdated state may be missing), or 'fetch-failed' (the repository query errored; the list is complete, outdated state is whatever an earlier fetch cached). This list carries no security vulnerabilities and no per-package detail; call positronPackages.getPackages for those. When there are no packages to report, an object with available: false and a reason of 'disabled', 'no-session', 'session-not-ready', 'unsupported', or 'failed' -- the last of which also carries a message.\n\n### `positronPackages.getPackages`\n\nReports **full detail** on the packages you name: the full description plus the\ndetail fields (license, author, source repository, publication date) and the\nsecurity vulnerabilities that `getAllPackages` leaves out. Pass an array of\nnames (matching is case-insensitive). Use it to look a package up rather than\nscanning the whole list, and to answer \"is X installed?\" reliably.\n\n**Reading the payload:**\n\n- `packages` holds the named packages that **are** installed, with full detail.\n- `notFound` holds the names that are **not** installed. A name here is a\n  definitive \"not installed\" -- that is the reason to name packages rather than\n  to search the compact list, which can be large.\n- `metadataStatus` and `vulnerabilityStatus` mean the same as elsewhere (see\n  above and the advisories section below).\n- The same `available: false` reasons apply. In addition, if you call it\n  without any names it returns `reason: 'no-names'` -- pass the package names.\n\n**Arguments:**\n- `names` (array of string): The package names to look up, as the package repository knows them (for example: dplyr, pandas). Pass an array of names, or a single name. Matching is case-insensitive.\n\n**Returns:** An object with available: true, the session the packages belong to, packages (the named packages that are installed, with full detail), notFound (the named packages that are not installed -- a name here is a definitive \"not installed\", not a truncated-away answer), metadataStatus (how the outdated state was obtained: 'fresh', 'cached', 'unsupported', 'timed-out', or 'fetch-failed'), and vulnerabilityStatus (how advisories were obtained). Each installed package carries name, version, latestVersion, outdated, attached, description, url, license, author, sourceRepository, publishedDate, title, and vulnerabilities. vulnerabilities are the security advisories against the installed version, worst first (id, osvId, score, scoreVersion, severity of 'critical'/'high'/'medium'/'low'/'unscored', summary, fixedIn, published, url); an empty array means the repository was asked and reports nothing against that version, which is an all-clear, while an absent field means there is no advisory data for that package at all, which is not. vulnerabilityStatus says how the advisories were obtained: 'fresh' (Package Manager queried now), 'cached' (the cached advisories were still current), 'disabled' (advisory lookups are turned off in settings), 'unavailable' (a lookup ran and produced nothing, which is not worth retrying), or 'timed-out' (the lookup ran out of time partway). vulnerabilitySource names the Package Manager host that served them and when it answered. When no packages are named, an object with available: false and reason 'no-names'. When there are no packages to report at all, an object with available: false and a reason of 'disabled', 'no-session', 'session-not-ready', 'unsupported', or 'failed' -- the last of which also carries a message.\n\n## Security advisories\n\n`getPackages` carries known security advisories against each named package's\ninstalled version, so a question about whether a package is vulnerable is\nanswered by `getPackages` -- not by a web search, and not by running an auditing\ntool. (`getAllPackages` omits advisories to stay compact, so name the packages\nyou care about and call `getPackages`.)\n\n**The three states of `vulnerabilities` are all meaningful, and conflating\nthem is the easiest mistake to make here:**\n\n- A non-empty array -- this installed version is affected.\n- An **empty** array -- the advisory host was asked and reports nothing\n  against this version. That is a genuine all-clear; say so.\n- **Absent** -- there is no advisory data for this package. Nothing can be\n  concluded either way. Do not report it as clean.\n\n**Reading an advisory:** entries are pre-sorted worst-first, so the first one\nis the headline and matches what the Packages pane shows the user. `severity`\nis always present (`critical`/`high`/`medium`/`low`/`unscored`) and is the\nfield to rank by. `unscored` means the advisory carries no CVSS score, which\nis common for CRAN's RSEC records -- it means \"vulnerable, severity unknown\",\nnot \"probably fine\". `id` is the CVE when one exists, otherwise the OSV id.\n\n**`vulnerabilityStatus`** is tracked separately from `metadataStatus` because\nthe two come from different places: outdated state from the runtime's package\nmanager, advisories from Posit Package Manager. Either can fail while the\nother answers, so check the one that matches the claim you are making. On\n`disabled`, `unavailable` or `timed-out`, do not tell the user they have no\nvulnerabilities -- you did not find out.\n\n**Whether to call again** -- the status tells you, and only one value is worth\na second call:\n\n- `fresh` or `cached` -- the advisory data is as complete as it gets. A package\n  with none was already looked up for you, so calling again returns the same\n  thing. Don't.\n- `timed-out` -- the lookup ran out of time partway. The package list is\n  complete, but some packages carry only what was cached, possibly nothing.\n  Calling again resumes where it stopped, so this is the one case where a\n  second call adds information.\n- `disabled` or `unavailable` -- no advisory data is coming. `disabled` means\n  the user turned advisory lookups off in settings; `unavailable` means the\n  lookup ran and produced nothing, because either no Package Manager here\n  reports advisories or the lookup failed. Neither is worth retrying: say what\n  you could not determine and stop.\n\n**Attribution:** when `vulnerabilitySource` is present, say where the data\ncame from (`host`) and when (`fetchedAt`). Advisory data has a date; presenting\nit as timeless fact overstates it.\n\n**Fixing one:** `fixedIn` is display text, and may name fixes on several\nrelease branches (`\"1.26.5, 2.0.2\"`). It is deliberately not\nmachine-comparable, so do not pass it to `updatePackage` as a version. Pick\none with the user, then update to that exact version. Do not reach for\n`updateAllPackages` to fix a single advisory.\n\n## Installing, updating and refreshing\n\n`installPackage` and `updatePackage` take the same argument pair: `name`, then\n`version`. For `version`, pass an exact version when the user named one,\n`'latest'` when they just want the newest. Read `version` back off the result\nto learn what `'latest'` actually resolved to, rather than predicting it or\ntelling the user a version you did not confirm.\n\nNever invent a package name from a partial request. If the user says \"install\nthe plotting one\", ask which.\n\n### `positronPackages.installPackage`\n\nInstalls a package that is not there yet. If the package is **already\ninstalled, this does nothing at all**, whatever `version` says -- it will not\nmove an installed package to a different version. Use `updatePackage` for\nthat. So look the package up with `getPackages` first: it tells you whether it\nis installed, and so which of the two commands the user actually needs.\n\nBase R installs ignore `version` entirely and always take the current release\nfrom the repository. Do not promise a specific version on an R session using\nthe base installer.\n\n**Arguments:**\n- `name` (string): Name of the package to install, as the package repository knows it (for example: dplyr, pandas).\n- `version` (string): Version to install: either an exact version (for example: 1.1.4) or 'latest' for the newest version available to the session. If the package is already installed, installing it again does nothing, whatever this is set to -- use the update command to move an installed package to a different version. Base R installs ignore this and always install the current release from the repository.\n\n**Returns:** An object with installed, name, version, and message. installed is true when the package was installed; version is then the version that was actually installed, read back from the session, which is how you learn which version 'latest' turned out to be. When installed is false, message explains why (a failed install, or a canceled install).\n\n### `positronPackages.updatePackage`\n\nMoves an already-installed package to a different version. Returns\n`updated: false` with a `message` when the installed version is already the\nnewest available -- that is a normal outcome, not an error; relay it rather\nthan retrying.\n\nAs with install, base R updates ignore `version`.\n\n**Arguments:**\n- `name` (string): Name of the installed package to update (for example: dplyr, pandas).\n- `version` (string): Version to update to: either an exact version (for example: 1.1.4) or 'latest' for the newest version available to the session. Base R updates ignore this and always install the current release from the repository.\n\n**Returns:** An object with updated, name, version, and message. updated is true when the package was updated, with name and version confirming what was requested (version is the concrete version the session reported as newest when 'latest' was passed); when updated is false, message explains why (the installed version is already the newest available, a failed update, or a canceled update).\n\n### `positronPackages.updateAllPackages`\n\nUpdates every installed package in the session to its latest available\nversion. Use when the user asks to update all their packages. This can take a\nwhile for a large environment -- say so before starting.\n\nPrefer `updatePackage` when the user named specific packages. Updating\neverything to fix one package is a much larger change than they asked for.\n\n**Arguments:** None.\n\n**Returns:** None.\n\n### `positronPackages.refreshPackages`\n\nRefreshes the Packages pane's list. Use when a package was installed or\nremoved outside Positron (from a terminal, say) and the pane looks stale.\n\nThis is for the *pane*. To read the installed list yourself, use\n`getAllPackages`, which reads live and does not need this first.\n\n**Arguments:** None.\n\n**Returns:** None.\n\n## Preconditions, and what a failure means\n\n`installPackage`, `updatePackage`, `updateAllPackages` and `refreshPackages`\nall share one precondition: the Packages pane must be enabled in settings,\n**and** a session must be active, **and** no package operation may already be\nrunning.\n\nThat last clause is the one to watch. A `disabled` failure does not\nnecessarily mean the feature is off or the session is missing -- it may simply\nmean an install or update is in flight. Wait and tell the user an operation is\nalready running; do not retry in a loop, and do not conclude packages are\nunavailable. `getAllPackages` and `getPackages` still work while an operation\nruns, so use one to tell the cases apart.\n\n## After installing or updating\n\nA newly installed or upgraded package often cannot be loaded until the session\nrestarts, because the old version may already be loaded in memory. Positron\nprompts the user about this itself, so do not pre-empt it.\n\nIf the user does ask you to restart, use\n`workbench.action.language.runtime.restartActiveSession` from\n[troubleshooting.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/references/troubleshooting.md) -- and tell\nthem first that a restart **discards all session state** (variables, loaded\npackages, history). Never restart silently as a cleanup step.\n\nTo show the user the result, focus the Packages pane with\n`workbench.view.positronPackages.view.focus` from\n[ui.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/references/ui.md).\n"},"elapsedMs":14}</script></tool-result></div>

<div><tool-result call-id="call_11etdlH9yyoS5hqfPAUhhUPr"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 3.1KB, 93 lines, showing lines 1-93]\n1\t/*\n2\t  ONS Census 2021: population processin...[truncated, total 3447 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 3.1KB, 93 lines, showing lines 1-93]\n/*\n  ONS Census 2021: population processing example\n  Source data: RM121, Sex by age, England and Wales (ONS).\n\n  This program imports the accompanying CSV, assigns broad age bands,\n  performs simple quality checks, and creates England-and-Wales totals and\n  percentages by sex and age band.\n\n  In SAS Studio: upload both files to the same folder, then replace data_dir\n  below with that folder's path.\n*/\n\n%let data_dir=/Users/alex/Documents/Codex/2026-11-19/ca/outputs;\n\nfilename onsin \"&data_dir./ons_rm121_sex_by_age_2021.csv\";\n\n/* Import explicitly so the program does not depend on PROC IMPORT guessing\n   column types or variable names from the CSV headers. */\ndata ons_population;\n    infile onsin dsd dlm=',' firstobs=2 lrecl=1048576 truncover;\n    length la_code $9 la_name $80 sex $6 age_band $30 age_group $6;\n    informat sex_code age_code population best32.;\n    format population comma15.;\n\n    input la_code :$9.\n          la_name :$80.\n          sex_code :best32.\n          sex :$6.\n          age_code :best32.\n          age_band :$30.\n          population :best32.;\n\n    /* Convert the ONS 23 age categories into common reporting bands. */\n    select (age_code);\n        when (1, 2)                     age_group = '0-4';\n        when (3, 4, 5, 6)               age_group = '5-15';\n        when (7, 8, 9)                  age_group = '16-24';\n        when (10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15,\n              16, 17)                   age_group = '25-64';\n        when (18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23)   age_group = '65+';\n        otherwise                       age_group = 'Unknown';\n    end;\n\n    if missing(la_code) or missing(sex) or missing(population) then delete;\nrun;\n\n/* Quality check: there should be no missing or negative counts. */\nproc sql;\n    title 'Data-quality check';\n    select count(*) as records format=comma12.,\n           sum(missing(age_group)) as missing_age_groups,\n           sum(population \u003c 0) as negative_counts\n    from ons_population;\nquit;\n\n/* Aggregate the local-authority records to England-and-Wales totals. */\nproc summary data=ons_population nway;\n    class sex age_group;\n    var population;\n    output out=population_by_age_sex(drop=_type_ _freq_) sum=population;\nrun;\n\nproc sql;\n    create table population_results as\n    select a.sex,\n           a.age_group,\n           a.population format=comma15. as population,\n           100 * a.population / b.total_population\n               as percent_of_sex format=5.1\n    from population_by_age_sex as a\n    inner join\n      (select sex, sum(population) as total_population\n       from population_by_age_sex\n       group by sex) as b\n    on a.sex = b.sex\n    order by sex, a.age_group;\nquit;\n\ntitle 'England and Wales population by sex and broad age group, Census 2021';\nproc print data=population_results noobs label;\n    label age_group='Age group'\n          percent_of_sex='Percent within sex';\nrun;\n\nproc sgplot data=population_by_age_sex;\n    vbar age_group / response=population group=sex groupdisplay=cluster;\n    yaxis grid label='Population';\n    xaxis label='Age group';\n    title 'Population totals by sex and broad age group';\nrun;\n\ntitle;\n"},"elapsedMs":2}</script></tool-result></div>

malformed records carry their parser diagnostics.\nread_population_text \u003c- function(path, encoding = \"UTF-8\", delimiter = \",\") {\n  if (!file.exists(path)) stop(paste(\"Input does not exist:\", path), call. = FALSE)\n  data \u003c- suppressWarnings(readr::read_delim(\n    path, delim = delimiter, quote = '\"', escape_double = TRUE,\n    col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),\n    locale = readr::locale(encoding = encoding), na = character(), trim_ws = FALSE,\n    name_repair = \"minimal\", skip_empty_rows = FALSE,\n    show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE, lazy = FALSE\n  ))\n  parse_issues \u003c- readr::problems(data)\n  if (nrow(parse_issues)) {\n    population_abort(\"Delimited-file parsing failed.\", population_issue(\n      \"P0-04\", paste0(\"Expected \", parse_issues$expected, \"; actual \", parse_issues$actual),\n      field = as.character(parse_issues$col)\n    ), data)\n  }\n  data\n}\n\n#' Import validated headers and preserve source field text.\n#'\n#' record_id is the logical data-record number, not necessarily the physical line.\ningest_population \u003c- function(config) {\n  raw \u003c- read_population_text(config$input_file_path, config$encoding, config$delimiter)\n  headers \u003c- names(raw)\n  expected \u003c- unname(config$columns)\n  if (anyDuplicated(headers) || !setequal(headers, expected)) {\n    population_abort(\"Input headers do not match the configured schema.\", population_issue(\n      \"P0-02\", paste0(\"Missing: \", paste(setdiff(expected, headers), collapse = \"; \"),\n                      \". Unexpected: \", paste(setdiff(headers, expected), collapse = \"; \"),\n                      \". Duplicate headers: \", anyDuplicated(headers) > 0)\n    ), raw)\n  }\n  canonical \u003c- raw[unname(config$columns)]\n  names(canonical) \u003c- names(config$columns)\n  canonical \u003c- tibble::add_column(canonical, record_id = seq_len(nrow(canonical)), .before = 1)\n  list(raw_data = raw, data = canonical)\n}\n\n#' Read and validate source-category reference tables before using them as rules.\nread_population_references \u003c- function(config) {\n  age \u003c- read_population_text(config$age_reference_path)\n  sex \u003c- read_population_text(config$sex_reference_path)\n  expected_age \u003c- c(\"source_age_code\", \"source_age_label\", \"age_group\", \"age_group_order\")\n  if (!setequal(names(age), expected_age) || anyDuplicated(names(age)) ||\n      !setequal(names(sex), c(\"sex_code\", \"sex_label\")) || anyDuplicated(names(sex))) {\n    stop(\"Category reference headers are invalid.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  for (reference in list(age, sex)) {\n    if (!nrow(reference) || any(vapply(reference, function(x) any(is.na(x) | trimws(x) == \"\"), logical(1)))) {\n      stop(\"Category references must be nonempty without missing fields.\", call. = FALSE)\n    }\n  }\n  if (anyDuplicated(age$source_age_code) || anyDuplicated(sex$sex_code) ||\n      anyDuplicated(age$source_age_label) || anyDuplicated(sex$sex_label)) {\n    stop(\"Category reference codes and labels must be unique.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (any(!grepl(\"^[1-9][0-9]*$\", age$age_group_order))) {\n    stop(\"Age-group order must contain positive integers.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  age$age_group_order \u003c- readr::parse_double(age$age_group_order)\n  groups \u003c- dplyr::distinct(age, age_group, age_group_order)\n  if (any(!is.finite(age$age_group_order)) || anyDuplicated(groups$age_group) ||\n      anyDuplicated(groups$age_group_order)) {\n    stop(\"Each age group must have a unique finite reporting order.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  list(age = age, sex = sex)\n}\n"},"elapsedMs":11}</script></tool-result></div>

Dependency locking is planned but has\nnot yet been initialised, so the existing R session/library is not replaced.\n\nBefore claiming routine acceptance, obtain the official geography reference and\nbenchmark or record an explicitly restricted, non-certified use decision. **Stage 1 is complete.** All 15,226 records passed the structural checks, with zero rejections. Nine automated test blocks also passed, covering schema changes, quoted fields, missing and invalid values, duplicates, incomplete category grids and reference integrity. The original CSV and SAS files are unchanged.

The setup is in [config/ons_rm121_2021.yml](config/ons_rm121_2021.yml), the decisions and instructions are in [docs/implementation_progress.md](docs/implementation_progress.md), and this run’s evidence is in [the run manifest](outputs/ons_rm121_sex_by_age_2021_input_20261119T121514_43141bb4871/manifest.json).

Next comes age grouping, aggregation and percentages. One output-policy decision matters before proceeding: official geography coverage and benchmark reconciliation are still blocked.

floor(population))) {\n+    stop(\"Population must contain finite nonnegative whole counts.\", call. = FALSE)\n+  }\n+  total \u003c- sum(population)\n+  if (!is.finite(total) || total > 2^53 - 1) {\n+    stop(\"Population total exceeds the exact numeric range.\", call. = FALSE)\n+  }\n+  total\n+}\n+\n+#' Aggregate a validated single-release dataset using explicit grouping keys.\n+#'\n+#' observation_keys describe the full source grain. Future period-aware adapters\n+#' must include period in both the observation keys and retained grouping keys.\n+aggregate_population \u003c- function(data, group_keys, observation_keys) {\n+  required \u003c- unique(c(group_keys, observation_keys, \"population\"))\n+  if (!length(group_keys) || !length(observation_keys) ||\n+      !all(required %in% names(data)) || \"population\" %in% c(group_keys, observation_keys) ||\n+      anyDuplicated(group_keys) || anyDuplicated(observation_keys) || !nrow(data)) {\n+    stop(\"Aggregation requires explicit valid keys and nonempty data.\", call. = FALSE)\n+  }\n+  if (anyNA(data[unique(c(group_keys, observation_keys))]) ||\n+      anyDuplicated(data[observation_keys])) {\n+    stop(\"Source observation keys must be nonmissing and unique.\", call. = FALSE)\n+  }\n+  # Known context dimensions may never be silently pooled across their values.\n+  context_keys \u003c- intersect(c(\"period\", \"release_id\", \"geography_version\", \"measure\",\n+                              \"sex_classification\", \"age_classification\"), names(data))\n+  for (key in setdiff(context_keys, group_keys)) {\n+    if (dplyr::n_distinct(data[[key]]) > 1L) {\n+      stop(paste(\"Aggregation would pool different values of\", key), call. = FALSE)\n+    }\n+  }\n+  before \u003c- safe_population_total(data$population)\n+  result \u003c- data |>\n+    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(group_keys))) |>\n+    dplyr::summarise(population = sum(population), .groups = \"drop\")\n+  if (safe_population_total(result$population) != before || \u003c- function(totals, group_keys, denominator_keys,\n+                                             tolerance = 1e-8) {\n+  if (!length(denominator_keys) || !all(denominator_keys %in% group_keys) ||\n+      !all(c(group_keys, \"population\") %in% names(totals)) ||\n+      anyDuplicated(totals[group_keys]) || anyNA(totals[group_keys]) || !nrow(totals)) {\n+    stop(\"Percentage keys must identify unique nonmissing groups and denominator dimensions.\", call. = FALSE)\n+  }\n+  if (!is.numeric(tolerance) || length(tolerance) != 1L || !is.finite(tolerance) ||\n+      tolerance \u003c= 0 || tolerance > 0.001) {\n+    stop(\"Invalid percentage tolerance.\", call. = FALSE)\n+  }\n+  safe_population_total(totals$population)\n+  denominators \u003c- totals |>\n+ Methodology and current limits\n+\n+This workflow preserves the reviewed SAS calculation, not its known defects.\n+Source counts represent authority–sex–age observations. The original text is\n+retained during ingestion; invalid records cause failure, not silent exclusion.\n+The category references are transcriptions of the supplied extract, not externally\n+authenticated ONS codebooks.\n+\n+Age codes 1–2 map to 0–4, 3–6 to 5–15, 7–9 to 16–24, 10–17 to 25–64,\n+and 18–23 to 65+. These are exact unions of source categories. No estimation or\n+splitting of counts is performed. Every mapping must be many-to-one and complete.\n+\n+Counts are summed across observed authorities within each sex and reporting age\n+group. A percentage is 100 times the group count divided by the sum across all\n+five groups for the same sex. The machine-readable result retains the denominator\n+and full-precision percentage. Round to one decimal place only when displaying;\n+the rounded male percentages total 100.1%, which is an expected rounding effect.\n+\n+The supplied-file regression expectations are female 30,420,281, male 29,177,325\n+and combined 59,597,606. All ten reviewed group counts are in\n+`tests/expected/ons_rm121_2021_results.csv`. These expectations are tied to the\n+source checksum in the tests. They are not independently verified official totals.\n+\n+CSV and PNG outputs are explicitly provisional and remain inside a run-specific\n+`review/` directory. The count chart uses separate sex panels with a shared\n+scale, so colour is not needed to identify sex. The age groups have unequal widths\n+and 65+ is open-ended; the bars are totals, not densities or counts per year of age.\n+\n+Geography coverage is checked only within observed authorities. No authoritative\n+geography list or comparable official benchmark has been supplied, so independent\n+coverage and official acceptance remain blocked. The geographical scope and year\n+are descriptions inherited from the supplied files, not external certification.\n+The workflow cannot promote itself to official acceptance by editing a status flag.\n+\n+Future adapters must validate their own source schemas and domains. Exact mappings\n+must respect classification boundaries. Source and grouping keys must retain\n+periods and other context that define separate populations. Do not sum snapshots,\n+overlapping geography levels, incompatible classifications, rates or percentages.\n\n--- README.md\n+++ README.md\n@@ -1,1 +1,44 @@\n-# AI-PoC\n\\ No newline at end of file\n+# AI-PoC\n+\n+## Population-processing workflow\n+\n+The R workflow replaces the reviewed SAS calculation with explicit ingestion,\n+validation, exact age mapping, aggregation and within-sex percentages. The\n+original files in [Inputs](Inputs/) are preserved unchanged.\n+\n+**Current outputs are provisional review artefacts, not accepted official totals.**\n+Only the supplied files are available; authoritative geography coverage and\n+official benchmark reconciliation remain blocked.\n+\n+### Running\n+\n+Use R with readr, dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2, yaml, digest and jsonlite installed. Tests\n+also require testthat. Dependency locking and clean-session verification are\n+planned; the existing session is not replaced or restarted automatically.\n+\n+Source [scripts/run_population_analysis.R](scripts/run_population_analysis.R),\n+then call `run_population_analysis(project_root)` with the explicit absolute\n+project-root path. It returns results and output paths invisibly. Input locations,\n+schema and settings are in [config/ons_rm121_2021.yml](config/ons_rm121_2021.yml).\n+Paths in configuration are relative to the supplied project root, never a\n+personal home directory. No interpolation,\n#' unknown bucket, row loss or multiplication is permitted.\nderive_population_age_groups \u003c- function(data, age_reference) {\n  keys \u003c- c(\"source_age_code\", \"source_age_label\")\n  required \u003c- c(keys, \"age_group\", \"age_group_order\")\n  if (!all(c(keys, \"population\") %in% names(data)) ||\n      !all(required %in% names(age_reference)) ||\n      any(c(\"age_group\", \"age_group_order\") %in% names(data))) {\n    stop(\"Age derivation requires unmapped validated data and a complete mapping schema.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (anyDuplicated(age_reference$source_age_code) ||\n      anyNA(age_reference[required]) || any(!nzchar(age_reference$age_group))) {\n    stop(\"Age mapping must have unique source codes and no missing categories.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  groups \u003c- dplyr::distinct(age_reference, age_group, age_group_order)\n  if (!is.numeric(groups$age_group_order) || any(!is.finite(groups$age_group_order)) ||\n      any(groups$age_group_order \u003c 1 | groups$age_group_order != floor(groups$age_group_order)) ||\n      anyDuplicated(groups$age_group) || anyDuplicated(groups$age_group_order)) {\n    stop(\"Age reporting groups must have unique positive integer ordering.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  unmatched \u003c- dplyr::anti_join(data, age_reference, by = keys)\n  if (nrow(unmatched)) {\n    population_abort(\"Age mapping contains unmatched source categories.\", population_issue(\n      \"P0-11\", \"No exact code-label match in the age mapping.\", unmatched$record_id,\n      \"source_age_code\"\n    ), data)\n  }\n  before \u003c- safe_population_total(data$population)\n  mapped \u003c- dplyr::left_join(data, age_reference[required], by = keys, relationship = \"many-to-one\")\n  if (nrow(mapped) != nrow(data) || safe_population_total(mapped$population) != before) {\n    stop(\"Age mapping did not preserve records and population.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  mapped\n}\n"},"elapsedMs":9}</script></tool-result></div>

Duplicate headers: \", anyDuplicated(headers) > 0)\n    ), raw)\n  }\n  canonical \u003c- raw[unname(config$columns)]\n  names(canonical) \u003c- names(config$columns)\n  canonical \u003c- expected_age \u003c- c(\"source_age_code\", \"source_age_label\", \"age_group\", \"age_group_order\")\n  if (!setequal(names(age), expected_age) || anyDuplicated(names(age)) ||\n \u003c- function(totals, group_keys, denominator_keys,\n                                             tolerance = 1e-8) {\n  if (!length(denominator_keys) || !all(denominator_keys %in% group_keys) ||\n \u003c= 0)) {\n    stop(\"Percentage denominator must be positive.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  result \u003c- totals |>\n    dplyr::left_join(denominators, by = denominator_keys, relationship = \"many-to-one\") |>\n    dplyr::mutate(percent_of_sex = 100 * population / denominator_population)\n  sums \u003c- result |>\n    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(denominator_keys))) |>\n <div><thinking id="thinking-1795090811887-0kjdl">
**Clarifying failure status**

I need to address the failure status issue regarding initial input validation conditions. It’s important to initialize before trying anything. In stage 1, after creating a hash, I capture and write data. Problems with read permission on the hash can lead to a loss of record or status. In stage 2, writing status before trying is key; however, if an error occurs during JSON read/save, stage 1 status might still remain in the system.


</thinking><span data-thinking-duration-ms="2002"></span></div>

## Findings

1. **Misleading chronology pass.** `R/ingestion.R:77–81` checks only that age-group orders are unique and finite. Swapping the orders of `0-4` and `65+` would still pass, produce a wrongly ordered chart and CSV, and report “Explicit chronological category order” as passed (`scripts/run_population_analysis.R:61–65`). The tests check the supplied mapping, but the runner does not enforce it.

2. **Percentages can pool periods silently in reuse.** `R/summarisation.R:51–75` permits a caller to omit `period` from denominator keys even when it is in the group keys. The resulting percentages pool periods and still pass the 100% reconciliation. The reuse test supplies the correct denominator but does not test this omission (`tests/testthat/test-calculations.R:61–72`).

3. **Manifest hashes may not identify the rules used.** The validation stage hashes configuration and references before reading them (`scripts/validate_population_input.R:23–31, 37–40`), then the analysis stage rereads both without verifying those hashes (`scripts/run_population_analysis.R:29–31`). An intervening edit can change the mapping or presentation while the manifest records the earlier files.

4. **Some failed runs are not marked failed.** Run-directory creation, hashing, session capture and the initial manifest write occur outside the validation error handler (`scripts/validate_population_input.R:21–37`). A failure there can leave a run directory without a failed manifest. The analysis-stage manifest read and initial update are also outside its handler (`scripts/run_population_analysis.R:21–28`).

The supplied configuration and output code keep official coverage, benchmark reconciliation and acceptance blocked. This was a read-only review; nothing was executed.
</SUBAGENT>

malformed records carry their parser diagnostics.\nread_population_text \u003c- function(path, encoding = \"UTF-8\", delimiter = \",\") {\n  if (!file.exists(path)) stop(paste(\"Input does not exist:\", path), call. = FALSE)\n  data \u003c- suppressWarnings(readr::read_delim(\n    path, delim = delimiter, quote = '\"', escape_double = TRUE,\n    col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),\n    locale = readr::locale(encoding = encoding), na = character(), trim_ws = FALSE,\n    name_repair = \"minimal\", skip_empty_rows = FALSE,\n    show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE, lazy = FALSE\n  ))\n  parse_issues \u003c- readr::problems(data)\n  if (nrow(parse_issues)) {\n    population_abort(\"Delimited-file parsing failed.\", population_issue(\n      \"P0-04\", paste0(\"Parser row \", parse_issues$row, \": expected \",\n                       parse_issues$expected, \"; actual \", parse_issues$actual),\n      field = as.character(parse_issues$col)\n    ), data)\n  }\n  data\n}\n\n#' Import validated headers and preserve source field text.\n#'\n#' record_id is the logical data-record number, not necessarily the physical line.\ningest_population \u003c- function(config) {\n  raw \u003c- read_population_text(config$input_file_path, config$encoding, config$delimiter)\n  headers \u003c- names(raw)\n  expected \u003c- unname(config$columns)\n  if (anyDuplicated(headers) || !setequal(headers, expected)) {\n    population_abort(\"Input headers do not match the configured schema.\", population_issue(\n      \"P0-02\", paste0(\"Missing: \", paste(setdiff(expected, headers), collapse = \"; \"),\n                      \". Unexpected: \", paste(setdiff(headers, expected), collapse = \"; \"),\n                      \". Duplicate headers: \", anyDuplicated(headers) > 0)\n    ), raw)\n  }\n  canonical \u003c- raw[unname(config$columns)]\n  names(canonical) \u003c- names(config$columns)\n  canonical \u003c- tibble::add_column(canonical, record_id = seq_len(nrow(canonical)), .before = 1)\n  list(raw_data = raw, data = canonical)\n}\n\n#' Read and validate source-category reference tables before using them as rules.\nread_population_references \u003c- function(config) {\n  age \u003c- read_population_text(config$age_reference_path)\n  sex \u003c- read_population_text(config$sex_reference_path)\n  expected_age \u003c- c(\"source_age_code\", \"source_age_label\", \"age_group\", \"age_group_order\")\n  if (!setequal(names(age), expected_age) || anyDuplicated(names(age)) ||\n = FALSE)\n    }\n  }\n  if (anyDuplicated(age$source_age_code) || anyDuplicated(sex$sex_code) ||\n      anyDuplicated(age$source_age_label) || anyDuplicated(sex$sex_label)) {\n    stop(\"Category FALSE)\n  }\n  age$age_group_order \u003c- readr::parse_double(age$age_group_order)\n  groups \u003c- dplyr::distinct(age, age_group, age_group_order)\n  if (any(!is.finite(age$age_group_order)) || Future period-aware adapters\n#' must include period in both the observation keys and retained grouping keys.\naggregate_population \u003c- function(data, group_keys, observation_keys) {\n  required \u003c- unique(c(group_keys, observation_keys, \"population\"))\n  if (!length(group_keys) || !length(observation_keys) ||\n      !all(required %in% names(data)) || \"population\" %in% c(group_keys, anyDuplicated(result[group_keys])) {\n    stop(\"Aggregation reconciliation failed.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  result\n}\n\n#' Calculate full-precision percentages using explicit denominator dimensions.\n#'\n#' Denominator keys must include period/context when those define separate totals.\n#' No rounding or missing-value removal is performed here.\ncalculate_population_percentages \u003c- function(totals, group_keys, denominator_keys,\n                                             tolerance = 1e-8) {\n  if (!length(denominator_keys) || !all(denominator_keys %in% group_keys) ||\n      !all(c(group_keys, \"population\") %in% names(totals)) ||\n      anyDuplicated(totals[group_keys]) || anyNA(totals[group_keys]) || !nrow(totals)) {\n    stop(\"Percentage keys must identify unique nonmissing groups and denominator dimensions.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  if (!is.numeric(tolerance) || length(tolerance) != 1L || !is.finite(tolerance) ||\n      tolerance \u003c= 0 || tolerance > 0.001) {\n    stop(\"Invalid percentage tolerance.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  safe_population_total(totals$population)\n  denominators \u003c- totals |>\n    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(denominator_keys))) |>\n    dplyr::summarise(denominator_population = sum(population), .groups = \"drop\")\n  if (any(denominators$denominator_population \u003c= 0)) {\n    stop(\"Percentage denominator must be positive.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  result \u003c- totals |>\n    dplyr::left_join(denominators, by = denominator_keys, relationship = \"many-to-one\") |>\n    dplyr::mutate(percent_of_sex = 100 * population / denominator_population)\n  sums \u003c- result |>\n    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(denominator_keys))) |>\n    dplyr::summarise(percentage_sum = sum(percent_of_sex), .groups = \"drop\")\n  if (any(!is.finite(result$percent_of_sex)) || any(abs(sums$percentage_sum - 100) > tolerance)) {\n    stop(\"Unrounded percentages do not reconcile to 100 within denominator groups.\", call. = FALSE)\n  }\n  result\n}\n"},"elapsedMs":8}</script></tool-result></div>

Do not create an HTML summary at this stage.\n\nOnly the supplied CSV and SAS files are available. Source URL, download date,\nrelease, exact reference date, geography vintage, population definition and an\nauthoritative benchmark are unknown. Do not infer these from the filename.\nIndependent national coverage and official-total acceptance remain blocked.\n\n## Checkpoint 1: ingestion and validation\n\nThe source files remain unchanged. Configuration paths are project-relative.\nThe supplied file is ASCII-compatible; UTF-8 is an appropriate reader setting for\nthis file, not a claim about all future downloads. Missing-value markers beyond\nempty fields are unconfirmed; observations must currently be unsigned decimal\ninteger text, without grouping separators or scientific notation. Zero is valid.\nNo data are trimmed, deduplicated, imputed or silently excluded.\n\nCategory reference tables were transcribed from the supplied file and reviewed\nSAS mapping. They are not independently sourced official codebooks. Completeness\nis checked within observed geographies: a wholly absent geography cannot be\ndetected without an external geography reference. Counts and a checksum in tests\nare regression fixtures only and are not universal processing requirements.\n\nTo run the input checkpoint, source `scripts/validate_population_input.R`, then\ncall `run_input_validation()` with the explicit project-root path. The function\nreturns validated data invisibly and writes a unique `outputs/` evidence folder.\nThe root path is supplied by the caller; processing does not change directories.\nNo population-results CSV or chart is produced until the next checkpoint.\n\nThe initial checkpoint was executed successfully against all 15,226 supplied\nrecords, with zero rejections. The automated tests cover schema changes, quoted\nfields, invalid counts, missing fields, duplicates, incomplete grids and reference\nintegrity. Test execution evidence is retained with the latest checkpoint run.\n\nRun automated tests from the project root with `testthat::test_dir(\"tests/testthat\")`.\nSet `PA_TEST_SCRATCH` to a writable scratch directory before running tests;\ntemporary fixtures belong there, not in the source-data directory.\n\n## Next checkpoints\n\nThe user approved provisional review exports while independent source evidence is\nunavailable. Exact category joins, total-preserving aggregation, full-precision\nwithin-sex percentages and chronological CSV/PNG outputs are now implemented.\nReview outputs are labelled provisional, and official acceptance remains blocked.\nThe chart uses separate sex panels and a shared scale instead of colour-dependent\nclustered bars. Full workflow test execution and rendered-chart inspection must\nbe completed before this checkpoint is treated as verified.\n\nRemaining hardening includes complete failure-publication tests, clean-session\nreproducibility and dependency locking. renv has not yet been initialised, so the\nexisting R session/library is not replaced.\n\nBefore claiming routine acceptance, obtain the official geography reference and\nbenchmark or record an explicitly restricted, non-certified use decision. A\nstructurally successful run is not an accepted official population result.\n"},"elapsedMs":17}</script></tool-result></div>

Do not create an HTML summary at this stage.\n\nOnly the supplied CSV and SAS files are available. Source URL, download date,\nrelease, exact reference date, geography vintage, population definition and an\nauthoritative benchmark are unknown. Do not infer these from the filename.\nIndependent national coverage and official-total acceptance remain blocked.\n\n## Checkpoint 1: ingestion and validation\n\nThe source files remain unchanged. Configuration paths are project-relative.\nThe supplied file is ASCII-compatible; UTF-8 is an appropriate reader setting for\nthis file, not a claim about all future downloads. Missing-value markers beyond\nempty fields are unconfirmed; observations must currently be unsigned decimal\ninteger text, without grouping separators or scientific notation. Zero is valid.\nNo data are trimmed, deduplicated, imputed or silently excluded.\n\nCategory reference tables were transcribed from the supplied file and reviewed\nSAS mapping. They are not independently sourced official codebooks. Completeness\nis checked within observed geographies: a wholly absent geography cannot be\ndetected without an external geography reference. Counts and a checksum in tests\nare regression fixtures only and are not universal processing requirements.\n\nTo run the input checkpoint, source `scripts/validate_population_input.R`, then\ncall `run_input_validation()` with the explicit project-root path. The function\nreturns validated data invisibly and writes a unique `outputs/` evidence folder.\nThe root path is supplied by the caller; processing does not change directories.\nNo population-results CSV or chart is produced until the next checkpoint.\n\nThe initial checkpoint was executed successfully against all 15,226 supplied\nrecords, with zero rejections. The automated tests cover schema changes, quoted\nfields, invalid counts, missing fields, duplicates, incomplete grids and reference\nintegrity. Test execution evidence is retained with the latest checkpoint run.\n\nRun automated tests from the project root with `testthat::test_dir(\"tests/testthat\")`.\nSet `PA_TEST_SCRATCH` to a writable scratch directory before running tests;\ntemporary fixtures belong there, not in the source-data directory.\n\n## Next checkpoints\n\nThe user approved provisional review exports while independent source evidence is\nunavailable. Exact category joins, total-preserving aggregation, full-precision\nwithin-sex percentages and chronological CSV/PNG outputs are now implemented.\nReview outputs are labelled provisional, and official acceptance remains blocked.\nThe chart uses separate sex panels and a shared scale instead of colour-dependent\nclustered bars. The full workflow has now been executed and the rendered chart\ninspected. All 17 automated test blocks pass, including a successful run followed\nby a failed input run and a failed zero-denominator run; previous results remain\nunchanged and both failure manifests are marked failed. These tests exposed and\nled to correction of an error-handler scoping defect before checkpoint completion.\n\nThe latest verified run is\n`outputs/ons_rm121_sex_by_age_2021_input_20261119T122347_4314ff90d17/`.\nIt retains all ten reviewed group counts, totals 59,597,606, and contains the\nprovisional CSV/PNG, validation evidence, test results and checksummed manifest.\nSource/reference/code changes during processing are detected, and reporting\norder is checked against the approved configuration. Known period/geography\ncontext cannot be omitted from percentage denominators.\n\nRemaining hardening includes export-failure and other edge-case integration\ntests, clean-session reproducibility and dependency locking. renv has not yet\nbeen initialised, so the existing R session/library is not replaced. Confirm the\nintended deployment systems and handover requirements before environment setup.\n\nBefore claiming routine acceptance, obtain the official geography reference and\nbenchmark or record an explicitly restricted, non-certified use decision. <div><tool-result call-id="call_0MhHErQ4KoP6xvbVSnqbmHav"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 2.3KB, 39 lines, showing lines 1-39]\n1\t# Methodology and current limits\n2\t\n3\tThis w...[truncated, total 2533 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 2.3KB, 39 lines, showing lines 1-39]\n# Methodology and current limits\n\nThis workflow preserves the reviewed SAS calculation, not its known defects.\nSource counts represent authority–sex–age observations. The original text is\nretained during ingestion; invalid records cause failure, not silent exclusion.\nThe category references are transcriptions of the supplied extract, not externally\nauthenticated ONS codebooks.\n\nAge codes 1–2 map to 0–4, 3–6 to 5–15, 7–9 to 16–24, 10–17 to 25–64,\nand 18–23 to 65+. These are exact unions of source categories. No estimation or\nsplitting of counts is performed. Every mapping must be many-to-one and complete.\n\nCounts are summed across observed authorities within each sex and reporting age\ngroup. A percentage is 100 times the group count divided by the sum across all\nfive groups for the same sex. The machine-readable result retains the denominator\nand full-precision percentage. Round to one decimal place only when displaying;\nthe rounded male percentages total 100.1%, which is an expected rounding effect.\n\nThe supplied-file regression expectations are female 30,420,281, male 29,177,325\nand combined 59,597,606. All ten reviewed group counts are in\n`tests/expected/ons_rm121_2021_results.csv`. These expectations are tied to the\nsource checksum in the tests. They are not independently verified official totals.\n\nCSV and PNG outputs are explicitly provisional and remain inside a run-specific\n`review/` directory. The count chart uses separate sex panels with a shared\nscale, so colour is not needed to identify sex. The age groups have unequal widths\nand 65+ is open-ended; the bars are totals, not densities or counts per year of age.\n\nGeography coverage is checked only within observed authorities. No authoritative\ngeography list or comparable official benchmark has been supplied, so independent\ncoverage and official acceptance remain blocked. The geographical scope and year\nare descriptions inherited from the supplied files, not external certification.\nThe workflow cannot promote itself to official acceptance by editing a status flag.\n\nFuture adapters must validate their own source schemas and domains. Exact mappings\nmust respect classification boundaries. Source and grouping keys must retain\nperiods and other context that define separate populations. Do not sum snapshots,\noverlapping geography levels, incompatible classifications, rates or percentages.\n"},"elapsedMs":5}</script></tool-result></div>

Verify on the intended Red Hat version without a display, including readable output and permissions.
2. **Reproducibility:** No lockfile or environment setup is present; `README.md:15–17` acknowledges this. Pin an R version and package versions, including directly used `tibble`; account for the native pipe and dplyr join `relationship` APIs (`R/category_mapping.R:30–32`). Document restore and system dependencies; retain the lockfile in version control while ignoring local library state (`.gitignore:1–7`).
3. **CLI:** Add a thin `Rscript` entry point with explicit root/config arguments, usage and nonzero failure exit status, without changing the working directory. Preserve the callable API and provisional-status contract (`scripts/run_population_analysis.R:9–13, 88–94`).
4. **Clean-process tests:** Launch the CLI in a separate clean R process from a different working directory, with scratch isolated from the source tree; assert exit status, artifacts and manifest. Current tests source functions into the test process, and their helper derives the root from the test working directory (`tests/testthat/helper-population.R:1–9`, `tests/testthat/test-run-safety.R:22–24`).
5. **Export failures:** Force CSV and PNG/storage failures deterministically and check failure status, diagnostics, partial artifacts and preservation of prior runs. CSV is written before PNG, so a failed run can retain partial review output (`scripts/run_population_analysis.R:60–66, 88–94`); consumers must not treat it as successful (`README.md:26–30`). Also test failures while writing the failure manifest or validation diagnostics: those writes can themselves fail and mask the original error (`scripts/validate_population_input.R:57–66`).
6. **Early failures:** Config loading, code hashing and run-directory creation occur before the relevant error handlers, so not every failure can produce a failed manifest (`scripts/run_population_analysis.R:14–28`, `scripts/validate_population_input.R:14–34`). Define and test the CLI’s diagnostic contract for these cases.
</SUBAGENT>

<div><tool-result call-id="call_cF4HqsaxdzhI410nV0gLAMNv"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 16.5KB, 266 lines, showing lines 1-110]\n1\t# Positron package commands\n2\t\n3\tReading,...[truncated, total 8736 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 16.5KB, 266 lines, showing lines 1-110]\n# Positron package commands\n\nReading, installing and updating the packages in an interpreter session. See\n[SKILL.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/SKILL.md) for how to call these commands and how to\nhandle failures.\n\nThe **Arguments** and **Returns** entries below are generated from the running\nbuild's command metadata, so they always match this Positron. The surrounding\nguidance is hand-written.\n\n## Read the environment, never probe it\n\nTo find out what is installed, what version it is, or whether something newer\nis available, call `positronPackages.getAllPackages` (the whole environment) or\n`positronPackages.getPackages` (specific packages, by name). **Do not run code\nto find out.** Writing `import pandas` in a try/except, calling `pip list`,\n`installed.packages()`, `importlib.metadata.version()`, or anything similar\nthrough `executeCode` is the wrong move every time: it runs code the user did\nnot ask for, it can have side effects (an import executes module-level code),\nit only answers for the one package you thought to test, and it tells you\nnothing about whether a newer version exists.\n\nThese commands have none of those problems. They change nothing, show the user\nnothing, and need no pane open. Reach for one before any package operation, and\nbefore answering any question about what the session has.\n\n**Which of the two to call:**\n\n- To size up the environment, or list what is installed, call\n  `getAllPackages`. It returns a compact entry per package, built to fit\n  hundreds of packages at once.\n- To look a package (or a few) up by name -- its full detail, its security\n  vulnerabilities, or simply *whether it is installed at all* -- call\n  `getPackages` with the names. A named package that is missing comes back in\n  `notFound`, which is a definitive \"not installed\"; the compact list can be\n  large, so do not conclude a package is absent just because you did not spot\n  it there.\n\n## Reading what's installed\n\n### `positronPackages.getAllPackages`\n\nReports every package installed in the foreground session, each with its\ninstalled version and whether a newer one is available. A **compact** list: the\n`description` is shortened to 256 characters (suffixed with `...` when cut), and\nsecurity vulnerabilities and the per-package detail fields (license, author,\nsource repository, publication date) are left out entirely to keep the whole\nenvironment inside the token budget. When you need the full description, the\ndetail fields, or the vulnerabilities for a package, call `getPackages` with its\nname.\n\nRead-only and quiet. Unlike the write commands below, this has **no\nprecondition** -- it is always callable, and tells you in its payload when it\nhas nothing to say. So a `disabled` failure from a write command does not mean\nyou cannot read.\n\n**Reading the payload:**\n\n- `available: false` comes with a `reason`, and each one calls for a different\n  response:\n  - `disabled` -- the user turned the Packages pane off in settings. Say so;\n    do not offer to turn it on by running code.\n  - `no-session` -- nothing is running, so there is no environment to\n    describe. Ask the user to start an interpreter.\n  - `session-not-ready` -- a session is starting up (or has exited). This one\n    is worth retrying shortly; the others are not.\n  - `unsupported` -- this runtime has no package manager. Nothing here will\n    work for it.\n  - `failed` -- the read itself failed; relay `message` rather than guessing.\n- `metadataStatus` says how far `outdated` can be trusted. Only `fresh` means\n  the repositories were queried just now. On `cached`, `timed-out` or\n  `fetch-failed`, report update information as possibly stale rather than\n  telling the user they are up to date. On `unsupported`, no package has\n  `outdated` at all, so its absence means nothing.\n- `session` names the session the answer describes. It is one session's\n  environment, not the machine's -- do not carry an answer across a session\n  switch or apply it to a different language.\n- `attached` is not the same as installed. A package can be installed but not\n  attached (not `library()`d in R, not imported in Python). \"Is pandas\n  available?\" is answered by the package appearing in the list at all;\n  `attached` only says whether it is on the search path right now.\n\n**Arguments:** None.\n\n**Returns:** An object with available: true, the session the packages belong to, the installed packages (name, version, latestVersion, outdated, attached, description, url) -- where description is shortened to 256 characters and suffixed with \"...\" when cut -- and metadataStatus saying how the outdated state was obtained: 'fresh' (repositories queried now), 'cached' (as of the last fetch), 'unsupported' (this runtime reports no outdated state, so no package has it), 'timed-out' (the list is complete but outdated state may be missing), or 'fetch-failed' (the repository query errored; the list is complete, outdated state is whatever an earlier fetch cached). This list carries no security vulnerabilities and no per-package detail; call positronPackages.getPackages for those. When there are no packages to report, an object with available: false and a reason of 'disabled', 'no-session', 'session-not-ready', 'unsupported', or 'failed' -- the last of which also carries a message.\n\n### `positronPackages.getPackages`\n\nReports **full detail** on the packages you name: the full description plus the\ndetail fields (license, author, source repository, publication date) and the\nsecurity vulnerabilities that `getAllPackages` leaves out. Pass an array of\nnames (matching is case-insensitive). Use it to look a package up rather than\nscanning the whole list, and to answer \"is X installed?\" reliably.\n\n**Reading the payload:**\n\n- `packages` holds the named packages that **are** installed, with full detail.\n- `notFound` holds the names that are **not** installed. A name here is a\n  definitive \"not installed\" -- that is the reason to name packages rather than\n  to search the compact list, which can be large.\n- `metadataStatus` and `vulnerabilityStatus` mean the same as elsewhere (see\n  above and the advisories section below).\n- The same `available: false` reasons apply. In addition, if you call it\n  without any names it returns `reason: 'no-names'` -- pass the package names.\n\n**Arguments:**\n- `names` (array of string): The package names to look up, as the package repository knows them (for example: dplyr, pandas). Pass an array of names, or a single name. Matching is case-insensitive.\n\n**Returns:** An object with available: true, the session the packages belong to, packages (the named packages that are installed, with full detail), notFound (the named packages that are not installed -- a name here is a definitive \"not installed\", not a truncated-away answer), metadataStatus (how the outdated state was obtained: 'fresh', 'cached', 'unsupported', 'timed-out', or 'fetch-failed'), and vulnerabilityStatus (how advisories were obtained). Each installed package carries name, version, latestVersion, outdated, attached, description, url, license, author, sourceRepository, publishedDate, title, and vulnerabilities. vulnerabilities are the security advisories against the installed version, worst first (id, osvId, score, scoreVersion, severity of 'critical'/'high'/'medium'/'low'/'unscored', summary, fixedIn, published, url); an empty array means the repository was asked and reports nothing against that version, which is an all-clear, while an absent field means there is no advisory data for that package at all, which is not. vulnerabilityStatus says how the advisories were obtained: 'fresh' (Package Manager queried now), 'cached' (the cached advisories were still current), 'disabled' (advisory lookups are turned off in settings), 'unavailable' (a lookup ran and produced nothing, which is not worth retrying), or 'timed-out' (the lookup ran out of time partway). vulnerabilitySource names the Package Manager host that served them and when it answered. When no packages are named, an object with available: false and reason 'no-names'. When there are no packages to report at all, an object with available: false and a reason of 'disabled', 'no-session', 'session-not-ready', 'unsupported', or 'failed' -- the last of which also carries a message.\n"},"elapsedMs":11}</script></tool-result></div>

<div><tool-result call-id="call_ocGx6sIF2b1KIJAAypymrWBU"><script type="application/json">{"version":1,"status":"success","result":{"type":"text","value":"[File: 8.5KB, 132 lines, showing lines 1-132]\n1\t# Positron session recovery commands\n2\t\n3\t...[truncated, total 9175 chars]"},"resultPreview":{"type":"code","value":"[File: 8.5KB, 132 lines, showing lines 1-132]\n# Positron session recovery commands\n\nRecovering a stuck interpreter session (Python, R, or another language) and\nshowing or reading help topics. See [SKILL.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/SKILL.md) for how to call\nthese commands and how to handle failures. To list the running sessions, switch\nbetween them, or start a new one, see\n[sessions.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/references/sessions.md). To list the available\ninterpreters or rescan for a newly installed one, see\n[interpreters.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/references/interpreters.md). For the packages\ninstalled in a session, see [packages.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/references/packages.md).\n\nThe **Arguments** and **Returns** entries below are generated from the running\nbuild's command metadata, so they always match this Positron. The surrounding\nguidance is hand-written.\n\n## Controlling the active interpreter session\n\nBoth commands below act on the *foreground* session -- whichever session is\nactive right now. That can be a console session or a notebook session (a\nnotebook's session is the foreground while its editor tab is focused), so these\nwork for notebooks just as well as consoles. Neither has a precondition, so both\nare always enabled; but when no session is running they do nothing and return no\nvalue rather than reporting `disabled`. So don't infer from a successful call\nthat something happened: if you're not sure a session is running, list sessions\nfirst (`getActiveSessions` in [sessions.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/references/sessions.md))\nand, if the list is empty, tell the user there's no session to act on instead of\nclaiming you interrupted or restarted one. To switch to a different session or\nstart a new one, see [sessions.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/references/sessions.md).\n\n### `workbench.action.languageRuntime.interrupt`\n\nInterrupts the active interpreter runtime session -- e.g., stops a running\ncomputation. Non-destructive: session state (variables, loaded packages) is\npreserved. Try this first when code appears stuck (an infinite loop, a\nlong-running call the user wants to cancel).\n\n**Arguments:** None.\n\n**Returns:** None.\n\n### `workbench.action.language.runtime.restartActiveSession`\n\nRestarts the active interpreter runtime session. **This discards all session\nstate** -- variables, loaded packages, and command history in that session are\nlost. Always tell the user this will happen before calling it, and prefer\n`interrupt` first when the goal is just to stop something running rather than\nto get a clean session.\n\n**Arguments:** None.\n\n**Returns:** None.\n\n## Looking up help topics\n\n### `positron.help.lookupHelpTopic`\n\nShows help for a topic -- typically a function or symbol name -- in the Help\npane. Uses the language of the active editor, or of the foreground interpreter\nsession if no editor is open. Requires a running interpreter session for that\nlanguage to actually resolve the topic.\n\nPass the topic exactly as the user names it (a bare function/symbol, e.g.\n`mean`, not a sentence). If the user hasn't specified a topic, ask before\ncalling. The command itself is always enabled, but expect a `found: false`\nresult (not `disabled`) if there's no running session for the relevant\nlanguage; relay the returned `message` rather than re-guessing the reason. To\nbring the Help pane into view after a lookup, use\n`workbench.panel.positronHelp.focus` from [ui.md](/Users/alex/Library/Application Support/Positron/User/globalStorage/positron.positron-skills/skills/positron-commands/references/ui.md).\n\n**Arguments:**\n- `topic` (string): Help topic to look up, typically a bare function or symbol name (for example: mean).\n\n**Returns:** An object with found, topic, languageId, and message. found is true when the help topic was shown in the Help pane, with topic and languageId confirming what was looked up and in which language; when found is false, message explains why (no topic provided, topic not found, no session for the language, or a lookup error).\n\n### `positron.help.readHelpTopic`\n\nReads the help page for a topic from a running interpreter session and returns\nit to you as Markdown, including signatures, arguments, details, and examples.\nNothing is shown to the user; use `positron.help.lookupHelpTopic` above when the\nuser wants to see the page.\n\nRead help before answering questions about how to call a specific function, what\nits arguments mean, or why a call is failing, and before writing code against a\npackage you don't know well. This is especially important for packages that are\nprivate, internal, or uncommon, since the installed help is the only reliable\nsource for them; it also reflects the exact version installed in the session.\n\nPass `languageId` (`r` or `python`) when the topic belongs to a language other\nthan the foreground session's. For R, pass the package in `package` rather than\nwriting `pkg::topic`. For Python, pass the import path as the topic (for example\n`pandas.DataFrame.merge`). If `found` is false, relay or act on `message`; for\nan R topic that is ambiguous or not found, retry with `package`.\n\n**Arguments:**\n- `topic` (string): Help topic to read: a function, class, or other object name (for example: mean, or pandas.DataFrame.merge).\n- `languageId` (string): Language of the package or topic, such as r or python. Defaults to the language of the foreground interpreter session.\n- `package` (string): Package containing the topic (for example: dplyr). Optional; when omitted, all installed packages are searched (R) or the topic is resolved as an import path (Python).\n\n**Returns:** An object with found, languageId, topic, package, content, and message. When found is true, content is the help page as Markdown, and topic and package identify the page that was read. When found is false, message explains why (no topic provided, no session for the language, topic not found, or a lookup error).\n\n### `positron.help.listPackageDocs`\n\nLists the documentation for an installed package: its help topics (with titles)\nand its vignettes, the long-form guides that explain a package's workflow. Use\nit to get oriented in a package you don't know, especially a private or internal\none, or when you need a help topic or vignette name you can't guess. For R,\neach topic's `aliases` are the function names it documents; pass one of those\nwith `package` to `positron.help.readHelpTopic`. For Python, topics are the\npackage's public members, given as full import paths, and the README is the only\nvignette.\n\n**Arguments:**\n- `package` (string): Name of the package (for example: dplyr or pandas).\n- `languageId` (string): Language of the package or topic, such as r or python. Defaults to the language of the foreground interpreter session.\n\n**Returns:** An object with found, languageId, package, topics, vignettes, and message. When found is true, topics lists help topics (topic, title, and for R, aliases naming the functions the topic documents) and vignettes lists vignettes (name and title). When found is false, message explains why (no package provided, no session for the language, package not installed, or a lookup error).\n\n### `positron.help.readVignette`\n\nReads a vignette and returns it as Markdown. Vignette names are not guessable,\nso get them from `positron.help.listPackageDocs` first. Read a vignette when the\nuser wants to learn how to use a package or asks about its intended workflow,\nrather than about a single function. Vignettes can be long, so read one only\nwhen it is relevant to the question.\n\n**Arguments:**\n- `package` (string): Name of the package (for example: dplyr).\n- `vignette` (string): Name of the vignette, as listed by positron.help.listPackageDocs (for example: colwise).\n- `languageId` (string): Language of the package or topic, such as r or python. Defaults to the language of the foreground interpreter session.\n\n**Returns:** An object with found, languageId, package, vignette, title, content, and message. When found is true, content is the vignette as Markdown (or its source, for vignettes without HTML output). When found is false, message explains why (missing arguments, no session for the language, vignette not found, or a lookup error).\n"},"elapsedMs":8}</script></tool-result></div>
